sections.h2: What is Suwannee County, and why do its parcels look different?
sections.html:
Suwannee County became Florida's 37th county on December 21, 1858, cut from the western part of Columbia County. The county's own history page says the river that gives it a name starts in the Okefenokee Swamp in south Georgia, winds about 240 miles and ends at the Gulf, with more than 70 springs along the way.

Live Oak grew up where the Pensacola and Georgia Railroad, begun in 1857 and finished in 1861, passed a large live oak tree and pond. Sawmills later defined the west side: a Dowling Park mill was one of the two biggest in Florida, and the same page says the county once turned out about 300,000 barrels of turpentine in a year. The Hal W. Adams Bridge to Mayo is described as the only suspension span in Florida.

The result for a seller is a mix of in-town lots, river and spring frontage, old farm tracts and mobile home sites. Legal descriptions and parcel numbers deserve a second look before any contract.

sections.h2: Who does what for a Suwannee County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser values land and buildings, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the taxing bodies set the rates. The appraiser's own page explains that the county commission, school board, city councils and water management district choose the tax rate, not the appraiser.

  • Property Appraiser: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak, phone 386-362-1385, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., closed on listed holidays including Good Friday and the Thursday and Friday of Thanksgiving.
  • Tax Collector: Live Oak office at 386-362-2816, serving Suwannee residents and making exceptions for property owners.
  • Planning and Zoning, which also handles flood plain questions: 224 Pine Ave. S.W., phone 386-364-3401.

The appraiser's site notes that working values can change daily until July 1, and that the 2026 rolls were certified, finally certified and post-VAB certified on notices posted June 24, October 7 and October 21, 2026.

sections.h2: Which filing dates matter for Suwannee owners?
sections.html:
March 1 is the big one for exemptions and special classifications, and April 1 is for business personal property. The collector adds a March 31 cutoff for indigent relief and for adjusting non-ad valorem assessments.

  • March 1: homestead, $5,000 disabled veteran, widow and widower exemptions, DR-501DV, DR-501M, agricultural classification (DR-482), conservation classification (DR-482C) and the conservation exemption (DR-418C).
  • June 1: financial information for the low-income senior exemption (DR-501SC).
  • April 1: tangible personal property return (DR-405).

Agricultural classification does not transfer. The appraiser states that a new application is needed when land changes hands, and that farm zoning alone does not earn the classification; the land must be in bona fide agricultural use on or before January 1.

sections.h2: What happens if a Suwannee County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Real estate takes a 3 percent penalty on April 1, and certificates are sold on unpaid accounts on or before June 1 with added charges. Business personal property accrues interest instead and may face a tax warrant.

The collector sets a firm rule on payment type: after April 30 only certified funds are accepted, and personal checks mailed or left in the drop box are returned. Card payments carry a 2.35 percent fee and are not taken by phone. A mailed payment is judged by postmark before April 1 and by date of receipt after.

A certificate holder may seek a deed two years after the April 1 of issuance. A buyer under a recorded contract for deed is among those notified before a tax deed sale, and homestead land has a higher opening bid. Ask the collector for a written payoff of every open year before listing.

sections.h2: How do Suwannee County installments and deferral work?
sections.html:
The quarterly plan needs an estimated bill above $100 and an application at the collector's office before May 1. It stays in force each year without a new form once the first payment is made on time.

Payments after June 30 and through July 31 are taken without a discount, and a missed first payment drops the parcel from the plan. Deferral is a separate tool for homesteads: the owner postpones the part above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent at 65 or older, and all of it under $10,000 of income ($12,000 at 70 or older). The mortgage may not exceed 70 percent of assessed value, total liens plus deferred tax may not exceed 85 percent, and applications are due January 31 after bills go out. The deferred tax becomes a lien.

sections.h2: Which Suwannee exemptions end with a sale?
sections.html:
All of them. Homestead requires that the home be in your name and your permanent residence on January 1, and Suwannee's list shows a $25,000 exemption plus $5,000 each for disabled veterans, widows, widowers, disabled persons and blind persons.

First-time applicants should bring a deed or contract, Florida driver's license and vehicle tag details and Social Security numbers. Veterans 65 or older with a combat-related permanent disability may get a discount equal to their VA percentage. A veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability may qualify for a full homestead exemption, which can carry to a surviving spouse married five years.

Under Save Our Homes the yearly increase is capped at the lower of 3 percent or inflation, but a sale resets the parcel to just value on the next January 1. If you plan another Florida purchase, ask about portability on Form DR-501T.

sections.h2: What local rules affect a Suwannee County house sale?
sections.html:
Check building history first. The county Building Department says the 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code and the 2023 National Electrical Code apply to permit applications from January 1, 2026. The department's phone is (386) 364-3407.

Mobile homes get special attention. Permits issued after May 1, 2022 require the pad to be inspected before the home is installed, and failure can mean the home is removed. Permits are not issued until all subcontractors have signed the addendum, and the driveway permit fee has been $50 since October 11, 2021.

Call Planning and Zoning with the parcel ID to learn whether the lot is in a flood plain zone. The appraiser's office can supply the parcel number.

sections.h2: What should I expect at the closing table?
sections.html:
The closing agent splits the current year's tax between buyer and seller by the closing date, and older unpaid years come out of proceeds. The collector asks sellers to forward the notice to the new owner or return it to the office.

The clerk records the deed and collects the state deed tax then. Afterward, ask the appraiser to update ownership and drop your exemption, and keep the signed closing statement for your records.

faqs.q: When did Suwannee County become a county?
faqs.a: It was formed on December 21, 1858, as the 37th Florida county, taken from the western portion of Columbia County.

faqs.q: What is the Suwannee County Property Appraiser's address?
faqs.a: The office is at 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak, FL 32064, phone 386-362-1385, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays except holidays.

faqs.q: Does Suwannee County let me pay property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if your estimated bill exceeds $100 and you apply before May 1. Four quarterly payments are due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

faqs.q: Can I defer Suwannee County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, for a homesteaded home with low income against the bill. Applications are due January 31 after bills are mailed, and the deferred amount becomes a lien.

faqs.q: Is agricultural classification transferable to a buyer in Suwannee County?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser says a new application is required after a sale, due March 1, and the land must be in bona fide agricultural use by January 1.
